floruit.note: The century the Russian calendar prints after his name, «Прп. Павла Препростого (IV)». The folder held no date at all before this reading.

death.note: One source of the four gives a year. The Serbian Ohrid Prologue, read 4 October 2026: «Скончао у дубокој старости, 340. год., и преселио се у радост ангелску.» days.pravoslavie.ru gives only the century, «Прп. Павла Препростого (IV)», which contains it; the Greek and Romanian entries for 7 March give none. The folder held the century and no year.

feast.note: The Russian keeps him on two days, the Julian 4 October and the Julian 7 March, behind one name page: 1697 is what the «Павла» of the 4 октября line links to and what the «Павла» of the 7 марта line links to. One row per church being the schema, the 4 October day is the row and the 7 March day is recorded here, and he does not render on the Russian 7 March. This note replaces one that said the Russian keeps him on 4 October where the Greek and the Romanian keep him on 7 March; that was a wrong claim and not an incomplete one.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, 4 октября ст. ст. — «Прп. Павла Препростого (IV).»
source.note: The rank is the alt text of the icon the page sets over the group of lines this one stands in, «Cовершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком» — a service the Typikon marks with no sign at all. The same calendar's line for 7 марта ст. ст. is «Прп. Павла Препростого (IV).», word for word the 4 октября line.

attestations.note: The Russian gives this folder its first date, the fourth century, and renders the epithet as one word, «Препростый» — the very simple one — where the Greek has ὁ ἁπλοῦς.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 7 martie — «Sfântul Cuvios Pavel cel Simplu»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Μαρτίου — «Όσιος Παύλος ο απλός»

attestations.note: The life page, https://www.saint.gr/3873/saint.aspx, has its own «Ημερομηνία Εορτής» of 7 Μαρτίου and «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή». It explains the epithet — he was called «απλός» because he was an unlettered farmer who knew nothing of the world's manners, yet was adorned with a guileless character, «τέλειος αγαθός ισραηλίτης, χωρίς καμμιά πονηριά και δόλο» — and says farming was his chief occupation until he was sixty. It tells of his wife, who had once been a servant in the city and played the noblewoman, mocked him as a fool and at last broke their marriage; that when he was sure of it he was filled with grief, groaned deeply, prayed, and decided to leave her and go far away; and that he went into the desert to Antony the Great, whose day the page gives as 17 Ιανουαρίου. It says he was given the gift of wonders and healed many possessed, and fell asleep in deep old age in the depths of the desert. It gives no year at all, and prints no hymn — only the distich «Γῆθεν μεταστὰς πρὸς Θεὸν Παῦλος Λόγον, / Τῆς ἁπλότητος πολλαπλᾶ στέφη λάβοι».

feast.note: Fourth of the four the Ohrid Prologue enumerates for this day. The Serbian church keeps him on 4 October with the Russian, where the Greek and Romanian keep him on 7 March; the days are not reconciled here, each church’s row carrying its own. The entry list drops this heading, which opens «Преп.»

source.text: Охридски пролог, 4. октобар ст. к. — «4. Преп. Павле Препрости. До своје 60. године живео у свету као жењен човек. … Скончао у дубокој старости, 340. год., и преселио се у радост ангелску.»
